newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian bonds open weaker amid softer currency.
newsitem.headline: Canadian bonds open weaker amid softer currency.

text.p: Canadian bonds opened weaker on Wednesday with a softer Canadian dollar and weakness in U.S. Treasuries weighing on prices, analysts said.

"It's mainly concern about the currency this morning. I don't think the numbers necessarily had so much to do with it, although they were pretty strong numbers," said Arve Bendiksrud, a fixed-income analyst with TD Securities Inc. "The fact that the U.S. market is a little bit weaker gives the Canadian market a bounce weaker as well."
Canada's 30-year benchmark bond fell C$0.21 to C$116.46 to yield 6.716 percent.
The U.S. 30-year bond fell 8/32 to yield 6.71 percent. The spread between the bonds narrowed to one basis point from two basis points at Tuesday's close.

The Canadian dollar opened weaker at C$1.3928 (US$0.7179) in after the unit traded in a narrow and weak range last night in overseas markets, trader said. The currency weakened further this morning to break past the key C$1.3950 level.

The currency trended weaker despite relatively positive economic data out this morning. Statistics Canada reported that average industrial weekly earnings rose a higher-than-expected 4.0 percent in April from a year earlier.
The government agency also reported that the country's leading indicator rose 0.7 percent in May from April. Economists had forecast the indicator would rise by 0.8 percent.
In other prices, Canada's 10-year benchmark bond fell C$0.27 to C$108.09 to yield 6.147 percent, compared to its U.S. equivalent which fell 8/32 to yield 6.44 percent.
The negative spread between the bonds was 29 basis points, unchanged from the close of trading on Tuesday.
The three-month cash T-bill yielded 2.83 percent against its U.S. equivalent which yielded 5.15 percent.
